_comment: EPISODE 3, TAKE C of three, THE PAYOFF. Answers only. THE PAYOFF IS ON THE FACE AND THE LINE, NOT ON A DRINK. `can_sealed` is off, so nothing may render an opening -- and drinking puts the can's LID at the person's mouth, which is the one thing keeping the can's state off screen (SKILL.md 31, 33). The format's own premise is that the strangers guess wrong and THE LAST ONE GETS IT RIGHT, so the last person simply knows. Episode 2 only tasted because its can was already open.

product._state_comment: The sealed grammar is OFF, as it is on take A. Two takes proved the clause does not render (SKILL.md 31) and the `upright` grammar keeps the LID OUT OF SHOT, so the can's state is never on screen. These two keys are the historic wording, back only because the sealed grammar is off; 'nobody opens a' still has to be written by something, and a person opening a can mid-shot is still its own defect.
